thread:
maria: FYI — ACME integration reported a regression after the canary this morning. They say tiny prompt edits that used to be no-ops now produce wildly wrong pricing values. Customer included a minimal repro. We escalated.

maria: Customer repro (they pasted this):
```
# original prompt (worked)
User: "What is the price for 10 units of product X?"
System: Provide price in USD only.

# tiny edit (now broken)
User: "What is the price for 10 units of product X? "  # note trailing space
System: Provide price in USD only.
```

maria: Old model returned: `USD 123.45` — new responses: `The product is not available` or hallucinated numbers like `USD 9999`. Customer says this started after the morning canary.

tara: Do we have a deploy timeline? Which rollout touched the preprocessor or tokenizer? :eyes:

deploy-bot: canary rollout: redwood-infer/v2.8.3 -> started 2026-03-15T08:12Z, completed on 4/5 nodes at 2026-03-15T08:25Z. No automatic rollback triggered.

vikram: @maria thanks. Can you paste the exact API request they used (headers + model + prompt_template param)? Need to check if we accidentally enabled prompt normalization/trim in the parser.

maria: Pasting sanitized request from logs: 
```json
{
  "api_key": "redacted",
  "model": "rid-gpt-medium-20260315",
  "prompt_template": "{{user_input}}\nSystem: Provide price in USD only.",
  "max_tokens": 60
}
```

maria: conversation id `conv-98765`, request id `req-6d2f`.

sarah: I ran a local parity test against `rid-gpt-medium-20260315` with both exact prompts. Repro confirmed: trailing space causes the policy/selector layer to route to a different tokenization path and the model picks a fallback safety response in some seeds.

sarah: Quick snippets from local run: 
```
prompt A -> "USD 123.45"
prompt B (trailing space) -> "We don't have that information"
```

vikram: That points to tokenizer normalization/whitespace handling change in this build. Our newer tokenizer merge rules may have created different subword boundaries causing the prompt template matcher to fail.

vikram: Short-term mitigation: we can pin ACME to `rid-gpt-medium-20260310` (previous variant) via customer routing, or update the Prompt Preprocessor to preserve trailing whitespace for template substitution. Which is faster?

tara: PM priority is to reduce customer impact. Pinning customer to previous model is fastest. We should also prepare a hotfix to preprocessor.

maria: Customer asked for a quick workaround on their side: add an explicit sentinel like `
---

` between user input and system line — that seems to avoid routing differences. They tried and it worked.

vikram: Ok I'll open an internal issue with repro, assign to runtime. Also want to check if quantization or kernel changes were introduced in v2.8.3 — sometimes that affects decoding in edge cases.

sarah: I pulled the build diff: only tokenizer_edges and a small patch to batching were changed. No quantization changes. Patch to tokenizer_edges added aggressive trim by default. That's likely the culprit.

sarah: Proposed hotfix: revert whitespace-trim flag or gate it behind an opt-in. Simple rollback patch ready. I'll draft PR.

monitor-bot: alert: error-rate spike + routing anomalies detected for rid-gpt-medium-20260315 between 08:20-08:28Z, +3.4x baseline.

tara: Good catch. Action items: 1) Pin ACME to previous variant (maria to coordinate). 2) Create urgent PR to revert tokenizer trimming (sarah/vikram). 3) Notify infra to hold full rollout until fix. 4) Send interim guidance to customer with workaround.

maria: On it — I'll apply routing pin and reply to customer with the sentinel workaround and offer to pin until fix is live.

vikram: I'll draft the GH issue and include logs/req ids. If QA gives green, we can do a targeted rollback of v2.8.3 canary nodes.

sarah: PR #4217 in progress. If we need emergency rollback, ping me and I can trigger rollback playbook.

maria: Thanks everyone. Will update thread after pin applied and customer notified. :rotating_light:

tara: Please add postmortem tag and link the customer ticket once done.

maria: Update: customer pinned and confirmed behavioral return to normal. Customer grateful but wants root cause timeline. We'll keep thread updated.
